analysis.title: YETI Holdings (YETI): Refreshing our brand momentum trackers and discussing key debates
key_insights: Ahead of 3Q results, GS refreshes its brand momentum trackers. Underlying brand metrics are healthy, but recent US demand indicators are sequentially more muted.
October retailer checks were constructive on the brand but most retailers noted a softer start to 4Q. Bestseller rankings, search momentum and observed transaction trends were mixed.
YETI reaffirmed its FY26 guidance at its late September Investor Day, which limits risk to F2H. International momentum remains strong.
GS believes US and drinkware growth in 3Q and 4Q will be critical for stock performance given toughening prior-year comparisons.

US drinkware is the key metric. Water bottle bestseller rankings are softer and search momentum across core categories is moderating. Management attributes the pressure to a few SKUs, a ~600bps drag on US drinkware growth in 2026, and expects it to subside later this year.

GS believes HSD growth overall and at least LSD-MSD% growth in the US is necessary for stock stability at current levels. Easy replenishment comparisons from last year and color launches could support demand, so the sell-in vs. sell-through balance is in focus.

The innovation pipeline is broad (phone cases, new bags, four-wheel luggage, a controlled test of technical apparel). GS checks on bags were more mixed and search interest in bags remains limited vs. core categories.
International growth is robust and led by Europe, from door expansion and higher productivity at existing doors. GS expects more consistency in F2H.

FY27 margin commentary is critical for the quarter. Inflation in stainless steel, resins, transportation and logistics continues to build, and tariffs are uncertain. The FY26 guide conservatively models a return to ~20% tariff rates.

GS believes YETI can deliver an algorithm margin expansion year in 2027 as Project Upcycle savings flow, but it is unclear whether management will guide to algorithm levels at the start of the fiscal year.
Brand health: purchase intent has tracked in line with peers, NPS remains above the peer set, and perceptions of durability, quality and warranty have improved relative to peers.
Pricing and promotion: Amazon Prime Day average markdown depth was 22% in October 2026 vs 29% in October 2025 and 25% at the June 2026 event. Selective price increases were taken in bags.
Cost trackers: ocean freight costs rose through 3Q, and stainless steel prices are above year-ago levels but moderating. YETI will lap an ~$8.2mn tariff-refund benefit in 2027, a Y/Y margin headwind.

GS cuts 2026/2027/2028 EPS to $2.98/$3.36/$3.89 from $3.00/$3.39/$3.92, citing moderation in domestic checks. It cuts its price target to $57 from $60 on a lower target EV/EBITDA multiple of 10.0x (from 10.5x), reflecting a lower revenue growth algorithm and higher 2027 cost risk. Rating stays Buy.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $57 from $60 on a lower target Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA multiple of 10.0x (from 10.5x) and slightly lower EPS estimates. Implies 17.9% upside from $48.33.

earnings_insights: YETI 3Q26 results are upcoming (not yet reported as of 11/4/2026). GS focus areas are US and drinkware growth and FY27 margin commentary.
GS estimates (not consensus): FY26E EPS $2.98 (old $3.00), FY27E $3.36 (old $3.39), FY28E $3.89 (old $3.92). FY25 actual EPS was $2.48.
GS estimates (not consensus): FY26E revenue $2,013.7mn (old $2,017.6mn), FY27E $2,162.9mn, FY28E $2,309.8mn. FY25 actual revenue was $1,868.5mn.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 3Q26E $0.87, 4Q26E $1.20, 1Q27E $0.32. 2Q26 EPS of $0.67 is shown as the prior quarter.
YETI reaffirmed its FY26 guidance at its late September Investor Day. The guide models a return to ~20% tariff rates.
GS FY26E EBITDA is $362.5mn and EBIT is $300.6mn, with EPS growth of 20.2% in 2026E.
risk_factors: Slower-than-expected growth in the core US market.
Increased competitive intensity in drinkware and adjacent categories, causing share pressure, higher promotions or reduced pricing power.
Weaker adoption of newer categories such as bags and packs, limiting diversification beyond drinkware.
Persistent tariff, freight, commodity or supply chain pressure limiting margin expansion and earnings growth.
Tariffs: the guide assumes a return to ~20% rates, while rates near 10%-12.5% would be a more favorable margin backdrop.

tension_points.bull_case: Management expects SKU-specific pressure (~600bps drag on US drinkware growth) to subside later this year. Replenishment comparisons are easy, color and innovation launches are at a record, international is strong, and NPS and quality perceptions are above peers.
tension_points.bear_case: Water bottle bestseller rankings and search momentum are softening, observed transactions are weaker, most retailers reported a softer start to 4Q, and bags search interest is limited.
tension_points.what_invalidates: US growth below LSD-MSD% (and total growth below HSD) in 3Q and 4Q would undermine stock stability at current levels.

tension_points.bull_case: Project Upcycle cost savings could deliver an algorithm margin expansion year in 2027, and tariffs near 10%-12.5% would be favorable vs the ~20% assumed.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation in steel, resin, freight and logistics is building, tariffs are uncertain, and YETI laps an ~$8.2mn tariff-refund benefit in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management declining to guide to algorithm margin levels, or Upcycle savings failing to offset input and freight inflation, in the 3Q call commentary on 2027.
